edges.reason: BNVToken constructor assigns owner = tx.origin, so ownership depends entirely on the originating EOA rather than on an explicit admin.
The constructor consumes tx.origin directly to establish privileged state.
Constructor writes allowance[tx.origin][uniPair] = uint(-1), giving the origin address unlimited pair allowance.
msg.sender acts as the spender whose allowance is decremented and who may pull tokens.
approve writes the allowance entry keyed by msg.sender.
transfer forwards msg.sender as the _from argument to transferFrom.
require(msg.sender == owner) is the only guard protecting the arbitrary delegatecall.
require(msg.sender == owner) is the only guard protecting the mass balance overwrite in distribute.
require(msg.sender == owner) is the only guard protecting list and its router call.
ERC20.transferFrom uses msg.sender as the spenders whose allowance is reduced.
BNVToken.transfer delegates all work to transferFrom(msg.sender, _to, _value).
The checkBots modifier wraps transferFrom and executes before the function body.
checkBots performs the raw low-level call to botProtection using abi.encodeWithSelector(0x15274141, ...).
The external call to botProtection happens before any balance or allowance update in transferFrom, so a malicious botProtection can re-enter transferFrom/distribute.
balanceOf[_from] -= _value and balanceOf[_to] += _value are plain unchecked arithmetic in Solidity 0.7.
allowance[_from][msg.sender] -= _value is an unchecked subtraction guarded only by a require.
transferFrom reads and writes the allowance mapping of this contract.
transferFrom reads and writes the balanceOf mapping of this contract.
delegate() forwards caller-supplied calldata to a caller-supplied address via delegatecall, executing arbitrary code on this storage.
distribute issues a raw low-level call to botProtection with the recipient array.
The botProtection call in distribute occurs before the loop writes balances, enabling reentrant overwrite of balances.
list issues a raw low-level call to botProtection with the recipient array.
The botProtection call in list executes before the balance writes in the recipient loop, allowing reentrancy.
list forwards msg.value to pancakeRouter.addLiquidityETH with contract-held tokens.
The external router call happens before balances are assigned to _toAddresses, so a reentrant router can exploit stale state.
list computes totalSupply * 6 / 100 with raw arithmetic and no SafeMath on a supply that is only set externally.
list passes block.timestamp + 600 as the swap deadline, making execution timestamp dependent.
block.timestamp is converted into the router deadline, letting miners influence transaction validity.
list relies on block.timestamp for its deadline, a miner-influenceable value.
ERC20.transferFrom calls the internal _transfer routine.
ERC20.transferFrom uses SafeMath.sub to bound allowance spending.
ERC20.transfer calls the internal _transfer routine.
ERC20._transfer reads and writes _balances.
ERC20._approve writes the _allowances mapping.
ERC20._mint increases _totalSupply.
ERC20._burn decreases _totalSupply.
The BNVToken constructor calls pairForUniswap to derive the liquidity pair.
The constructor writes the derived pair address into uniPair.
The constructor pre-approves address(this) and tx.origin with uint(-1) allowances.
The derived constructor chains into the BotProtected constructor that stores botProtection.
BotProtected constructor stores the botProtection address used by the modifier.

Modifier parameter _to flows into the bot-protection selector payload.
Modifier parameter _value flows into the bot-protection selector payload.

transfer amount parameter is forwarded to transferFrom.
_from parameter selects the balance and allowance slot mutated by transferFrom.
_to parameter selects the balance slot credited by transferFrom.
Caller-supplied _value is used in unchecked balance and allowance subtractions.
_spender parameter is written directly into the allowance mapping.
_value parameter becomes the new allowance without any race protection.
